The paired-load proposals have the clearest local code-generation and exact-sample evidence, but they are repeated versions of the same experiment; test one representative first, then avoid spending separate runs on duplicates. The two output-store proposals also describe the same change. I rank that change first because both local probe assembly and the supplied implementation report support testing it, while neither establishes GEMM speed. B-panel packing targets the incumbent’s strided B loads, but adds packing work and a 64 KiB panel. The new AC baseline varies widely, so no historical timing establishes a gain or causality. The proposed k_loop_schedule is last: its wording updates only two ZA tiles at each of two k steps, which appears to omit required tile updates; resolve that correctness ambiguity before testing. Its alternate ordering also is not shown to reduce stalls by the supplied compiler blocks.
